model: Broker FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (bank-style, net debt held at zero, engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Net proceeds of the 6 Aug 2026 H-share placement to CITIC Financial Holdings (803,725,383 H shares at HK$23.13; net HK$18.413bn = ~RMB15,848m at the filing's own conversion), completed after the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and retained offshore to capitalise CITIC Securities International/CLSA
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim report, 'Use of proceeds' and 'Changes in share capital'; carried at book since the capital is expected to earn roughly its cost

historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from FY2022->FY2025 (3y) and FY2020->FY2025 (5y). 'fcf' CAGRs are on profit attributable to owners (the FCFE numerator), not reported FCF, which is meaningless for a broker-dealer (FY2025 -45.5bn). Equity 5y CAGR (12.0%) is inflated by the FY2022 A+H rights issue (shares 12,927m -> 14,821m, ~RMB27bn); the 3y organic figure (8.1%) is the better anchor and is within 30% of revenue/EPS, so no divergence warning. The FY2025 base year was a strong market year (A-share average daily turnover +70%), so the 3y rates are measured trough-to-peak; through-cycle nominal growth for a scale broker is mid-single digit, which is what the driver paths fade to.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 is the cycle peak: revenue +27% to ~RMB134bn on H1's +44%, pre-tax margin 43%, attributable profit ~RMB44bn (ROE ~12-13% on the enlarged base). FY2027-28 give back 11% of revenue as A-share turnover and investment-income marks normalise, the margin settles at 37% (top of the FY2021-25 range, held by the fee-mix shift to ChinaAMC/wealth management and scale), and growth fades to 3% nominal. Through-cycle ROE ~9.5% versus a 10.5% cost of equity, so fair value sits a little under pro-forma book (RMB23.5/sh): the FCFE stream of ~RMB24-29bn/yr capitalised at 7.5% (10.5% - 3%) plus the placement cash. The business compounds book at 5-6% while paying out ~55% of earnings in capacity terms; actual payout is lower (~30-35%) and the surplus is credited as value-neutral retention.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-26 upswing is the start of the structural re-rating Beijing is engineering: consolidation toward ~10 leading institutions, pension pillars past RMB1tn, Stock Connect flows, and the RMB16bn CLSA recapitalisation lift international revenue past a quarter of the group. Revenue +38% in FY2026 with only a shallow FY2027 dip, a 40% pre-tax margin, ROE ~12%, terminal growth 3.5%. CITIC Securities earns above its cost of equity, so the value moves above book (~1.2x) - where the A-share already trades.
scenario_narratives.bear: The boom reverses: a policy move to cool speculative turnover, or a market fall that flips the RMB770bn FVTPL book's marks. Revenue -20% in FY2027 and -8% in FY2028 (a harsher replay of FY2022-23), pre-tax margin 32-33%, fee-rate reform and the merged rivals (Guotai Haitong, CICC+Dongxing+Cinda) cap the recovery at 2.5% growth. ROE ~7% against a 10.5% cost of equity: the FCFE stream is ~RMB12-17bn and the equity is worth ~0.5x book, the 2023-24 trough rating for the sector.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A broker's value is its through-cycle return on equity against its cost of equity, not a snapshot of a boom year. CITIC Securities is the scale leader and state champion of a sector Beijing wants to consolidate, and it has earned ~9.5% on equity across the last cycle - about its cost of equity - so fair value is close to book. FY2026 earnings (likely ~RMB44bn, ROE ~12-13%) are a cycle high built on +70% A-share turnover, and the model fades them rather than capitalising them. The H-share at ~0.77x pro-forma book and ~6.5x FY2026E earnings prices a cycle reversal; the A-share at ~1.1x book prices the reform story. The valuation sits between, nearer the H.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle reversal: 37% of FY2025 revenue was mark-to-market investment income on a RMB770bn FVTPL book; a market fall reverses it (bear case -20% revenue in FY2027).
Policy: CSRC levers on IPO pace, margin rules, stamp duty and fund fee-rate reform can cut brokerage, IB and AM revenue abruptly.

Retention earning below cost of equity: actual payout ~30-35% means the company keeps compounding book at 8-9%/yr; if the retained capital (including the RMB16bn CLSA injection) earns 7% rather than 9.5-10%, value falls toward the bear case regardless of the cycle.
Consolidation: a CITIC-CSC Financial tie-up (speculative, unconfirmed) would bring dilution and integration risk; merged rivals could take underwriting share.
Currency: value is built in CNY and bridged at 1.1747 HKD/CNY; CNY depreciation lowers the HKD value one-for-one.
A/H discount: the H-share may stay at a ~40% discount to the A-share indefinitely; the model does not assume the discount closes.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 6030.HK at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 20.04-32.50. CNYHKD=X and 600030.SS from the same API at the same time.
data_sources.financials: 6030.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-FY2026 interims; RMB millions). Share count, placement terms, H1 2026 P&L and equity from 6030.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (lines 4076-4092, 4300-4310, 4654-4663, 1445). ROE, net capital, DPS and tax from 6030.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (lines 1133-1136, 1069, 2380-2386, 10441-10456).

inputs.share_count_basis: 15,624,272,212 shares in issue after the 6 Aug 2026 H-share placement (12,200,469,974 A + 3,423,802,238 H; H1 2026 interim report, 'Financial Indicators Subsequent to the End of the Reporting Period'). No share options or restricted-share plan, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: the placement is already in the count and its cash is in the equity bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme or expense disclosed in the FY2025 annual report (no 'share-based payment' note; SOE-controlled A+H broker). SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in RMB (CNY) millions; H-shares quote in HKD. fx_rate 1.1747 HKD per CNY (model -> quote), Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-23. No parity check available: the A-share (600030.SS, CNY 25.45 at the same time) trades ~41% above the H-share on a common-currency basis, the usual A/H premium for mainland financials, so the A line is a reference, not a check. The placement's own conversion (RMB16.0bn = HK$18.59bn, i.e. 1.162) is within 1% of the rate used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CNY, because the flows are FCFE (profit attributable to owners less retained capital) and the model holds net debt at zero. China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + 6.5% equity risk premium for a mainland financial x beta 1.3 (H-share beta to HSI ~1.2-1.4; earnings are pro-cyclical with A-share turnover and 37% of FY2025 revenue is mark-to-market investment income) = 10.25%, rounded up to 10.5%. Same rate as China CITIC Bank (0998.HK, 10.5%): a securities firm's earnings are lower quality (trading book, cycle) but its balance sheet carries no NPL book, net capital is RMB157bn (210% of risk capital reserves) and the state parent just injected RMB16bn. Below 1788.HK's 11.5% (small HKD broker on 12x leverage). Same rate in all three scenarios so cycle risk is charged once, through the margin/growth paths and the probability weights, not twice through the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (RMB2.57bn at FY2025, notes 43) are immaterial against RMB2.08tn of assets and their cost is inside the pre-tax margin; not deducted again. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are profit attributable to OWNERS OF THE PARENT. The engine's PBT x (1 - rate) must land on attributable NI, so cash_tax_rate_path is the combined income-tax + NCI leakage on PBT: FY2024 23.6%, FY2025 24.5% (tax 8,816 + NCI ~931 on PBT 39,823), H1 2026 23.3% (tax 6,547 + NCI 544 on PBT 30,434). Statutory PRC rate 25%; the group's effective tax runs ~22% on tax-exempt fund and bond income. NCI equity (RMB5.98bn, mainly ChinaAMC and CITIC Futures minorities) is therefore not deducted separately (charged once, through the flow).
inputs.notes: MODEL: securities-broker FCFE capitalised at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine with the bank mapping used on 1788.HK, 0998.HK, 2016.HK, WF and LYG. ROUTING: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes financial institutions away from the owner-FCF DCF; a broker-dealer's reported operating cash flow (FY2024 +95.8bn, FY2025 -44.0bn, H1 2026 -42.0bn) swings with repo, margin-loan and client balances and says nothing about owner earnings, and 'net debt' (CSV total_debt 248.6bn of borrowings/bonds/short-term notes vs cash 144.0bn, plus 690bn of client brokerage deposits) is balance-sheet funding, not a claim to deduct from an earnings-based value. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue (fee + interest + investment income, CSV 'Revenue'; FY0 = FY2025 RMB105,333m); ebitda_margin_path = PRE-TAX PROFIT margin (da, sbc and lease paths = 0 so EBIT = PBT); cash_tax_rate_path = tax + NCI leakage (see nci_treatment); capex_pct_path = EARNINGS RETAINED to grow the equity base and regulatory net capital (the broker's reinvestment), set so terminal retention x terminal ROE = terminal growth; wc_capture_pct = 0. FCFE = attributable NI - required retention = dividend capacity. The company's ACTUAL payout is lower than this capacity (FY2025 34.5%, FY2024 35.5%; H1 2026 interim 28% of H1 EPS) - it has been compounding book at 8-9%/yr organically and earning ~9.5% ROE on it, roughly its cost of equity, so the surplus retention is value-neutral and the FCFE is credited as if distributable. The RMB16bn Aug-2026 placement completed AFTER the 30 June balance sheet: it is carried in equity_bridge at net proceeds (not in the June equity and not in the flows), while shares_outstanding is the post-placement count - both sides of the transaction are in, once each. last_fcf = FY2025 attributable NI 30,076 less retention required for 5.5% equity growth on opening equity 293,109 (16,121) = 13,955; FY2025 dividends actually paid to owners were 10,374 (RMB0.70/sh). NET DEBT = 0 by the bank convention. No SBC. Mid-cycle ROE: FY2021-25 average 9.45% (12.07/8.67/7.81/8.09/10.59); H1 2026 7.81% unannualised (~15% annualised) is a cycle high on +70% A-share turnover and is NOT the run-rate.

bear.growth_note: FY2026 +15% (~RMB121bn): H2 2026 falls back sharply from H1 (a policy move to cool speculative trading, or a market reversal). FY2027 -20% and FY2028 -8% replay the FY2022-23 post-boom decline (revenue -9% then flat, investment income -22%) at a harsher amplitude with FVTPL marks reversing; 2-3% nominal thereafter.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin falls to 33%/32% (FY2023 trough was 33.9%) and settles at 33%: fee-rate reform caps brokerage and fund fees, merged rivals (Guotai Haitong, enlarged CICC) take share, and the FY2025 gearing rise (79%) leaves a larger funding bill against a smaller revenue base.
bear.capex_note: Terminal retention 8.7% of revenue = 36% of NI (NI = 33% x 0.755 = 24.9% of revenue); retention x terminal ROE 7% = 2.5% growth. ROE below cost of equity means value sits well below book.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +27% (~RMB133.8bn): H1 2026 revenue 68.1bn (+44% YoY); H2 2025 was 57.5bn, so an H2 2026 that only matches H1 2025's level plus modest growth (~66bn) gives +27%. Then the cycle turns: -8% and -3% in FY2027-28 as A-share turnover and investment-income marks normalise from a +70% turnover year, back to 4% nominal (wealth-management AUM, ChinaAMC, international) fading to 3%.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin. FY2026 43% vs H1 2026 actual 44.7% (operating leverage on a trading boom); FY2027 39%, then 37% = the FY2021-25 range top (37.8-37.9% in FY2021/FY2022, 33.9% trough FY2023, 35.0% FY2024, 37.8% FY2025) held because the mix is shifting toward asset-management fees and scale is rising.
base.capex_note: Retained earnings as % of revenue. FY2026 14.5% = ~RMB19.4bn = 44% of NI = 5.5% equity growth (payout ~56% vs actual ~30-35%: the gap is surplus retention credited to FCFE, see inputs.notes). Glides to 8.9% of revenue = 31.7% of terminal NI (NI = 37% x 0.76 = 28.1% of revenue) so that retention x terminal ROE 9.5% = terminal growth 3.0%.

bull.growth_note: FY2026 +38% (~RMB145bn): H2 2026 runs at H1's pace. Only a shallow -3% dip in FY2027 because capital-market reform (National Nine Articles, pension pillars, Stock Connect flows) keeps turnover structurally higher; 5% nominal thereafter fading to 3.5%.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: 40% through-cycle: the consolidation-driven share gains and ChinaAMC/wealth fee mix lift the margin two points above the historical top.
bull.capex_note: Terminal retention 8.8% of revenue = 29% of NI (NI = 40% x 0.76 = 30.4% of revenue); retention x terminal ROE 12% = 3.5% growth. Implied payout ~71%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. The upside (structural reform plus consolidation leadership) and the downside (cycle reversal from a +70%-turnover year with a mark-to-market trading book as the largest revenue line) are both real and roughly equally likely from a cycle-high starting point; the state-parent backstop (RMB16bn injection in 2026) removes the solvency tail but not the earnings tail, so no tilt either way.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
